# Real slicer output

These four files are real OrcaSlicer output. They were not written or edited by hand. The
`real-fixtures` workflow (`.github/workflows/real-fixtures.yml`) made them on a GitHub Actions
Ubuntu 24.04 runner on 2026-11-25 with `slice_fixtures.py`, and the files here are that run's
artifact, unchanged. `provenance.json` records each file's SHA-256 (checked by
`tests/test_real_fixtures.py`), the OrcaSlicer build and its SHA-256, the profile names, and the
exact command line.

| File | Printer profile | Process | Filaments | Models |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `p1s-bead.gcode.3mf` | Bambu Lab P1S 0.4 nozzle | 0.20mm Standard @BBL X1C | Bambu PLA Basic, `#FFFFFF` | bead |
| `a1-bead.gcode.3mf` | Bambu Lab A1 0.4 nozzle | 0.20mm Standard @BBL A1 | Bambu PLA Basic, `#FFFFFF` | bead |
| `a1-mini-bead.gcode.3mf` | Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle | 0.20mm Standard @BBL A1M | Bambu PLA Basic, `#FFFFFF` | bead |
| `p1s-two-colour.gcode.3mf` | Bambu Lab P1S 0.4 nozzle | 0.20mm Standard @BBL X1C | PLA Basic `#FFFFFF` (bead), PLA Matte `#161616` (tile) | bead + tile |

The profiles are each printer's defaults in OrcaSlicer 2.4.2: the 0.4 mm nozzle, its default
process and its default filament (BBL profile bundle 02.01.00.19). The `@BBL X1C` process is
what OrcaSlicer selects for the P1S.

## How they were made

- **Models:** print-forge v0.2.0 (this account's own MIT project),
  `print-forge bead --preset gem-12` (a 12 mm faceted bead) and
  `print-forge letter --preset tile-7 --ascii` (a 22 mm letter tile).
- **Slicer:** OrcaSlicer 2.4.2, the release's
  `OrcaSlicer_Linux_AppImage_Ubuntu2404_V2.4.2.AppImage`, SHA-256
  `d12fb8c8eac1aecd2dfb6377acd48f994f8fa439ed5292fa532dd82880f029fd`, extracted with
  `--appimage-extract` and run headless under `xvfb-run`.
- **Profiles:** the OrcaSlicer command line does not resolve `inherits` for filament profiles
  (the filament fields stay at their defaults), and a machine profile whose parent is not
  resolved makes it fail. `slice_fixtures.py` therefore merges each system profile with its
  parents into one file and passes those. It also writes the colour into each filament profile
  as `filament_colour`; without it, OrcaSlicer ignored `--load-filament-ids` and sliced
  everything with the first filament.
- **Command** (per file; `$WORK` is a temporary directory):

  ```console
  orca-slicer --datadir $WORK/datadir --slice 0 \
    --load-settings "$WORK/<name>/machine.json;$WORK/<name>/process.json" \
    --load-filaments "$WORK/<name>/filament1.json[;$WORK/<name>/filament2.json]" \
    [--load-filament-ids 1,2] --arrange 1 --outputdir $WORK/<name>-out \
    --export-3mf <name>.gcode.3mf <models>
  ```

- **Reproducible:** the workflow slices again on every change to this folder and compares the
  plate G-code with these files, ignoring only the `; generated by OrcaSlicer 2.4.2 on <date>`
  header line. On Linux two runs gave identical G-code apart from that line. A Windows run of
  the same build differs only in the object ids in the `; printing object ... id:` comments,
  which there look like memory addresses.
- No plate thumbnail is written: headless OrcaSlicer reports "OpenGL context unavailable; skip
  thumbnail generating".

## Licences

OrcaSlicer is AGPL-3.0 and is only run in CI as a tool. Nothing of it is in this repository
except what it writes into its output. Each `.gcode.3mf` contains the resolved printer, process
and filament settings (`Metadata/project_settings.config`, and the `; CONFIG_BLOCK` in the
G-code) and the printers' start and end G-code templates, which come from OrcaSlicer's BBL
profiles (AGPL-3.0, derived from Bambu Studio's profiles). Those parts of these files are
therefore under AGPL-3.0, not this repository's MIT licence. They are test data that the code
only reads; no code here is derived from them. The models are print-forge output (MIT).

## What the analyser sees in them

From `gcode-insight analyze` at 0.4.0 (also asserted in `tests/test_real_fixtures.py` where
marked):

| File | Layers (tested) | Slicer filament | gcode-insight filament | Slicer model time | Model estimate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| p1s-bead | 59 | 219.88 mm, 0.67 g | 326.1 mm, 0.99 g | 277 s | 354.9 s (+28.1%) |
| a1-bead | 59 | 210.35 mm, 0.64 g | 333.3 mm, 1.01 g | 440 s | 473.1 s (+7.5%) |
| a1-mini-bead | 59 | 212.47 mm, 0.64 g | 327.2 mm, 0.99 g | 417 s | 426.9 s (+2.4%) |
| p1s-two-colour | 59, 20 tool changes | 1250.37 + 1041.36 mm, 3.79 + 3.31 g | 1463.0 + 1238.9 mm, 8.37 g | 2214 s | 1149.0 s (-48.1%) |

- **Filament.** gcode-insight counts every millimetre pushed, including the start G-code's
  nozzle purges and, in the two-colour file, the flushes at each filament change, because that
  filament leaves the spool. On the P1S bead it counts 106.2 mm more than the slicer's
  `filament used [mm]`, close to the 105 mm of the `G1 E50`, `G1 E50` and `G1 E5` purge moves
  in the P1S start G-code, so the slicer's figure appears to leave those out (an inference, not
  something OrcaSlicer documents). On the A1 and A1 mini beads the difference is 123.0 mm and
  114.7 mm; their start G-code has different purge moves, and the split was not worked out.
- **Time.** "Slicer model time" is the header's `model printing time`, the slicer's estimate
  without the start-up sequence. The model estimate is this tool's motion model, which ignores
  heating, homing, levelling and AMS filament changes; for the two-colour file the slicer
  allows for 20 filament changes and the model does not. Neither figure has been compared with
  a real print.
- **Tool changes.** The start G-code loads the filament of the first object printed (here the
  tile, filament 2), so the first change is reported as `T0 -> T1` during start-up: the analyser
  assumes tool 0 at the start of a file.
- The header also has `M73 P<percent> R<minutes>` progress lines, which gcode-insight does not
  read yet.

## Regenerating

Run the `Real slicer fixtures` workflow (Actions tab, "Run workflow"), download its
`real-fixtures` artifact and replace the files here with its contents. Locally, with an
OrcaSlicer 2.4.2 install and print-forge v0.2.0:

```console
python tests/fixtures/real/slice_fixtures.py --orca <orca-slicer> \
  --profiles <orca>/resources/profiles/BBL --out out
python tests/fixtures/real/slice_fixtures.py --check out
```
